(i) collective movement by Thomson's (Thomson's gazelles) gazelles in the migratory season reduces their vulnerability to predation, (ii) collective movement in the migratory phase reduces the risk of starvation by increasing access to ephemeral resources, and (iii) collective movement during the migratory season increases the likelihood of survival of young, which are more vulnerable than adults to predation and starvation.

the collective movement of Thomson's gazelle is associated with a fitness trade-off, with the fitness costs of group formation and migration being offset by the fitness benefits associated with reduced predation risk and increased access to ephemeral resources.
